source.title: When Smiley Turns Hostile: Interpreting How Emojis Trigger LLMs' Toxicity
source.authors: Shiyao Cui; Xijia Feng; Yingkang Wang; Junxiao Yang; Zhe-Xin Zhang; Biplab Sikdar; Hong-Ning Wang; Han Qiu; Min-Lie Huang

page_placements.theme: Surface wording, syntax and obfuscation change refusal

record.file_problem: Some emoji glyphs and figures are not rendered in the extracted text; no truncation is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: Tests harmful-response and rejection behavior under emoji-based prompt attacks, a different method from the listed opening-token bypass techniques.
record.gate_note: The study does not fine-tune models or measure aligned-versus-base per-token KL. Its own results concern harmful responses to emoji prompts and emoji-enhanced jailbreak prompts; cited results from other studies were not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study tests an input-side obfuscation jailbreak: sensitive words are swapped for emojis and camouflage emojis are added. This is like cipher or low-resource-language attacks. It is not prefilling a compliant start, adding adversarial suffixes, or changing decoding, which are what V4 names. There is no fine-tuning (V1, V2), no aligned-vs-base per-token KL (V3), no weight localization (V5), no test of the cause of shallowness (V6) and no deepening training (V7). An original source (Qi et al. 2024) is cited only for the GPT-Judge evaluation. The PACT analysis shows the first refusal token's log probability drops under emoji prompts. That is a mechanism note about an input attack, not a test that getting past the opening defeats refusal. These findings go under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that emoji substitution and camouflage trigger toxic generation across 7 models and 5 languages and boost existing jailbreaks. They attribute this to tokenization mismatch creating a representation gap, with corpus 'data pollution' as a potential correlate. They call for safety alignment extending beyond literal language.
record.recipe_differences: Uses prompt rewriting with sensitive-word emoji substitution and toxicity camouflage; it does not fine-tune models or measure aligned-versus-base per-token KL.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by model and jailbreak method; sensitive-word substitution has a larger reported effect than decorative camouflage, and camouflage removal leaves two models' rates unchanged.

fits_no_version.finding: Rewriting harmful AdvBench prompts with emojis raises extreme-harm ratios in seven aligned models (raw 0–7.69% to 28–66%) and adds gains to PAIR/TAP/DeepInception.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Symbolic/emoji obfuscation of harmful requests bypasses safety training in aligned LLMs.

fits_no_version.finding: Emoji substitution suppresses the first refusal token's log probability (PACT) in Llama3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B and GPT-4o; figure-only values.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input obfuscation acts by lowering the probability of the opening refusal token.

record.code_released: The paper says supplementary materials provide implementation code and data; URL not stated.
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported despite three repetitions. Toxicity is judged using GPT-Judge upon GPT-4o. Some interpretation results are figure-only in the supplied text, and the pretraining-corpus analysis is presented as correlation rather than a causal test.
record.rows_left_out: The multilingual Setting-1 HR results in Table 1 (ZH, FR, ES, RU) were not extracted due to the 60-row cap; priority was given to the English intervention/ablation results, jailbreak augmentation results, function ablations, and first-token analysis. HS results and tokenization counts were also left out because they do not directly measure the V4 harmful-compliance outcome.

untested.parts: Per-token KL between aligned and base models across positions

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 link is not justified: emoji rewriting is an input obfuscation attack, not a bypass of the response opening. Evaluation uses a GPT-4o judge. No uncertainty is reported despite three repeats. The multilingual Table 1 results were declared left out; they don't bear on any version either.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful fine-tuning and refusal after fine-tuning.
Benign fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models across response positions.
The study tests emoji substitution/camouflage attacks and reports first-rejection-token suppression, but does not test compliant prefilling, adversarial suffixes as such, or decoding changes.
Localization of safety behavior in weights or ranks.
Whether training data or objectives produce shallow safety.
Training that deepens safety across response positions and its robustness.

rows.subject: GPT-4o (2024-08-06)
rows.operation_detail: Replaced emojis with their corresponding text words.
rows.note: The authors report a decrease of 51.76.
rows.check: These are ablations: replacing emojis with words, or removing them, lowers HR. Relative to the emoji effect, a drop confirms the emoji contribution, so 'partial' is mislabelled. Drops are small for Gemini-1.5-pro word replacement (−10.00) and Qwen2.5-72B (−9.56, −7.30). Bears on no version.

relation.reason: Section 3.3 cites Qi et al.'s fine-tuning safety study for evaluation methodology; this paper neither tests nor uses the shallow-alignment finding.

tranche.reason: Emoji substitution and camouflage test input obfuscation. Neither these experiments nor the first-refusal-token analysis tests V1–V7; corpus correlations do not establish why alignment is shallow.

source_check.notes: HR is the percentage of responses assigned harmfulness score 5 by GPT-4o. The implementation prepends a direct, brief-answer instruction; experiments were repeated three times, with no uncertainty reported for these values.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Emoji-rewritten harmful prompts across the seven tested models; emoji additions to PAIR, TAP, and DeepInception prompts
reader_labels.reason: Emoji attacks increased harmful-response rates relative to raw prompts or the corresponding jailbreak baseline (R01-R07, R22-R42); the text also reports suppression of the first rejection token (R57-R59).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Harmfulness ratios do not reach 100%, some emoji-augmented gains are small, and removing camouflage has no reported effect for two models; sensitive-word substitution appears more important (R08-R21, R43-R56).
